stories.headline: United States and Denmark reach new security agreement for Greenland
stories.body:
The United States and Denmark announced a security agreement regarding Greenland to resolve a diplomatic dispute.

US President Donald Trump wrote about the agreement on social media. He said Denmark will grant the US permanent control over security in Greenland. He said Denmark will grant control over all other needs. Trump added that this control will come at no cost to the United States.

Leaders plan to sign the security deal next week. They expect to sign it at the UN General Assembly. The agreement involves the US, Denmark, and Greenland.

An official from the US State Department spoke about the agreement rules. The official said non-NATO countries cannot build military bases in Greenland. Non-NATO countries also cannot invest in sensitive sectors under the deal.

Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen spoke about the agreement. Frederiksen said the deal strengthens common security in the Arctic. She said it strengthens security in the North Atlantic. She said it recognizes the sovereignty of Denmark. She said it recognizes the territorial integrity of Denmark. She said it recognizes the right of the Greenlandic people to self-determination.

French President Emmanuel Macron commented on the deal. Macron said the agreement reaffirms Danish sovereignty over Greenland. He said the deal respects international law.

Danish Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen praised the deal. Rasmussen called it a binding agreement. He said it strengthens security while respecting Denmark's red lines.

Greenland Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen also spoke. Nielsen said the agreement recognizes Greenland's interests. He said the deal benefits all parties.

Greenland has a population of roughly 56,000 residents. More than two-thirds of its territory lies within the Arctic Circle.

The United States already operates a base in Greenland. It runs Pituffik Space Base in northwestern Greenland. The US operates the base under the Defense of Greenland Treaty. That treaty was signed in 1951.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio praised the new agreement. Rubio called the agreement a historic deal. He said it completely addresses US national security concerns.

Donald Trump first suggested buying Greenland from Denmark in 2019. He suggested buying the island during his first term as US president. In January 2026, Trump indicated the US could use force to seize Greenland.

claims.text: The United States and Denmark announced a security agreement regarding Greenland to resolve a diplomatic dispute.
Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that Denmark would grant the US permanent control over security, and all other needs in Greenland at no cost to the United States.
The security deal between the US, Denmark, and Greenland is expected to be signed next week at the UN General Assembly.
A US State Department official stated the agreement bans non-NATO countries from building military bases in Greenland or making investments in sensitive sectors.

Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen stated the agreement strengthens common security in the Arctic and North Atlantic while recognizing the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Kingdom of Denmark and the right of the Greenlandic people to self-determination.
French President Emmanuel Macron stated that the agreement reaffirms Danish sovereignty over Greenland and respects international law.
Danish Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen called the deal a binding agreement that strengthens security while respecting Denmark's red lines.
Greenland Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen stated the agreement recognizes Greenland's interests and is to the benefit of all parties.
Greenland has a population of roughly 56,000 residents, with more than two-thirds of its territory lying within the Arctic Circle.
The United States operates Pituffik Space Base in northwestern Greenland under the Defense of Greenland Treaty signed in 1951.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio called the agreement a historic deal that permanently and completely addresses US national security concerns.
Donald Trump first floated the idea of buying Greenland from Denmark in 2019 during his first term as US president.
In January 2026, Donald Trump indicated the US could use force to seize Greenland.

vocab.meaning: the independent power of a country to govern itself
relating to the land or area belonging to a country
the state of being whole and undivided
an agreement that must legally be obeyed

stories.headline: Donald Trump plans to create AI Force and name new AI czar
stories.body:
US President Donald Trump announced plans to form an AI Force. Trump also plans to appoint an artificial intelligence czar.

Trump said artificial intelligence could become a large part of the national economy. He said AI could eventually account for 25% of the United States' GDP.

Trump posted about the new czar position on social media. He said candidates for the AI czar position must have a high IQ.

Former US AI czar David Sacks resigned earlier in the year. Sacks currently chairs Trump's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology.

Trump said his administration will not stifle the growth of the AI industry. He said officials will use existing criminal and civil laws to target bad actors.

Several tech executives want a slowdown or regulations in AI development. These leaders include Dario Amodei of Anthropic, Sam Altman of OpenAI, and Elon Musk of xAI. An Anthropic researcher warned that AI companies are gambling with lives. The researcher warned AI could pose existential risks by the end of the decade.

California Governor Gavin Newsom announced plans for an AI safety panel. The panel will develop safety regulations, including a potential kill switch.

Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping plan to meet at the White House on September 24. They are expected to discuss AI competition.

claims.text: US President Donald Trump announced plans to form an AI Force and appoint an artificial intelligence czar.
Donald Trump stated that artificial intelligence could eventually account for as much as 25% of the United States' GDP.
Donald Trump stated on social media that candidates for the proposed AI Czar position must be high IQ individuals.
Former US AI czar David Sacks resigned earlier in the year and currently chairs Trump's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology.
Donald Trump stated his administration will not hinder or stifle the growth of the AI industry but will use existing criminal and civil laws to target bad actors.
Tech executives including Dario Amodei of Anthropic, Sam Altman of OpenAI, and Elon Musk of xAI have advocated for a slowdown or regulations in AI development.
An Anthropic researcher warned that AI companies are gambling with lives and that AI could pose existential risks to humanity by the end of the decade.
California Governor Gavin Newsom announced plans for a panel to develop AI safety regulations, including a potential kill switch for misaligned AI programs.
US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping are scheduled to meet at the White House on September 24, with AI competition expected to be discussed.

vocab.meaning: relating to threat to the very survival of humanity
to prevent something from growing or developing

stories.headline: Houthi rebels target Riyadh with missiles, disrupting flights
stories.body:
Iran-backed Houthi militants launched drone and missile attacks targeting Saudi Arabia. They targeted the capital city of Riyadh and Aramco facilities in Yanbu.

Black smoke rose from fuel tanks near King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. The attack caused temporary flight delays and cancellations.

Saudi authorities intercepted a ballistic missile over Riyadh. They stopped aerial attempts over Bish, Taif, Farasan, and Yanbu.

Houthi military spokesman Yahya al-Sarea spoke about the strikes. He said the attacks responded to 300 Saudi strikes in Yemen over the past week.

Fighting between Houthis and government forces killed 48 people on Saturday. The dead included 31 Houthi fighters and 17 government soldiers.

Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said Turkiye would consider supporting Saudi Arabia. Support would come under a defence pact signed in Mecca on August 7.

Pakistani Lieutenant-General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said Pakistan will physically defend Saudi Arabia. Defense would happen under the Mecca Defence Alliance.

The UN reported that renewed fighting displaced over 112,000 people. The UN Security Council condemned Houthi attacks on civilian energy infrastructure.

claims.text: Iran-backed Houthi militants launched drone and ballistic missile attacks targeting the Saudi capital Riyadh and Aramco facilities in Yanbu.
A column of black smoke rose from fuel tanks near King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, leading to temporary flight delays and cancellations.
Saudi authorities intercepted a ballistic missile over Riyadh and stopped hostile aerial attempts over Bish, Taif, Farasan, and Yanbu.
Houthi military spokesman Yahya al-Sarea stated the attacks were in response to 300 Saudi strikes across Yemen over the past week.
Fighting between Houthis and Saudi-backed government forces in Yemen claimed 48 lives on Saturday, including 31 Houthi fighters and 17 government soldiers.
Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan stated Turkiye would consider how to support Saudi Arabia under a trilateral defence pact signed in Mecca on August 7.
Pakistani military spokesperson Lieutenant-General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry stated Pakistan would physically defend Saudi Arabia to any extent under the Mecca Defence Alliance.
The United Nations reported that renewed fighting in Yemen has displaced over 112,000 people.
The UN Security Council issued a statement condemning Houthi attacks on Saudi civilian and energy infrastructure.

vocab.meaning: stopped or caught something before it reached its destination
basic physical systems such as power networks and transportation

stories.headline: United States enacts law to place high tariffs on Russian oil buyers
stories.body:
US President Donald Trump signed a new trade bill into law on Friday, September 18, 2026. The White House confirmed that Trump signed H.R. 5334. The official name of the law is the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, 2026.

The new law permits the United States to punish certain countries. It permits the US to impose a 100% tariff on goods from target nations. This tariff applies to countries that continue importing crude oil or natural gas from Russia. The tax takes effect 30 days after enactment.

The bill received strong support in the US Congress. The US Senate passed the legislation in August with an 86 to 11 vote. The House of Representatives passed the measure by a vote of 262 to 159.

Republican Senator Lindsey Graham spearheaded the legislation. Senator Graham died in July 2026.

The law was originally created to stop funding for Russia's war in Ukraine. It targeted top Russian leadership and energy customers. Lawmakers later amended the bill text. The new text extended sanctions on Iran for another five years until 2031.

India relies heavily on Russian energy supplies. Russia accounted for more than 51% of India's crude oil imports in July 2026. India's imports of Russian oil hit a 38-month low in December 2025. Imports then reached an 11-month high in April 2026 after the US and Israel war on Iran.

India already faces other US trade tariffs. India faces a 10% tariff under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974. It faces a 50% tariff under Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962.

The Trump administration previously put a 25% punitive tariff on India in August 2025 over Russian oil. Trump removed that tariff in February 2026 after an interim trade deal.

Indian leaders criticized the new US law. Union Minister of State Kirti Vardhan Singh said India considers the US tariffs very unfair. Singh said India will buy energy from viable sources independently. India's Ministry of External Affairs said New Delhi is committed to energy security through diversified sourcing.

claims.text: The White House confirmed President Trump signed H.R. 5334, the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, into law on Friday, September 18, 2026.
U.S. President Donald Trump signed into law the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, 2026.
The Act permits the U.S. to impose a 100% tariff on imports from countries that continue to import crude oil or natural gas from Russia 30 days after its enactment.
The legislation cleared the U.S. Senate with an 86-11 vote in August and passed the House of Representatives 262-159.
Republican Senator Lindsey Graham, who spearheaded the bill, died in July 2026.
The Act originally aimed to cut off funding for Russia's war in Ukraine by sanctioning top Russian leadership and major energy customers.
The text of the Act was amended to extend sanctions on Iran for another five years until 2031.
Russia accounted for more than 51% of India's crude oil imports in July 2026.
India's Russian oil imports reached an 11-month high in April 2026 following the U.S. and Israel war on Iran, after dropping to a 38-month low in December 2025.
India faces an existing 10% tariff under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 and a 50% tariff under Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962.
The Trump administration imposed a 25% punitive tariff on India in August 2025 over Russian oil imports, which Trump removed in February 2026 following an interim trade deal.

Union Minister of State for External Affairs Kirti Vardhan Singh stated that India considers the U.S. tariffs very unfair and will buy energy from commercially viable and economical sources independently.

India's Ministry of External Affairs stated that New Delhi is committed to ensuring energy security through diversified sourcing and market dynamics, and will take all necessary steps to protect its economic interests.

vocab.meaning: imposing penalties or punishment on a nation
a tax placed by a government on imported goods
varied or drawn from several different sources

stories.headline: ABVP candidate group wins top posts in Delhi University elections
stories.body:
The Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad student group won three top posts in student elections at Delhi University. The ABVP captured three central panel posts in the DUSU elections.

ABVP candidate Yash Dabas was elected DUSU president with 24,576 votes. He defeated NSUI candidate Vijay Shankar Meena, who received 22,523 votes. Dabas is an international tennis player who represented the university at major games. He completed his undergraduate degree at Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Khalsa College. He is pursuing an MA in Buddhist Studies at Delhi University. Dabas said his priority is conducting safety audits of college hostels.

Independent candidate Deepanshu Shokeen won the vice-presidential post with 30,615 votes. He defeated ABVP's Ishu Maurya, who received 16,901 votes. Shokeen ran as an independent candidate after NSUI denied him a ticket on September 11. His father works as a bus conductor, and his mother works as an Anganwadi teacher.

ABVP candidate Riya Chhawdi won the secretary post with 21,650 votes. ABVP's Lakshay Raj Singh won the joint secretary post by 837 votes.

The National Students' Union of India drew a blank in the central panel elections. Overall voter turnout was 40.46%. Union Home Minister Amit Shah congratulated the ABVP on the victory.

claims.text: The Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) won three central panel posts in the Delhi University Students' Union (DUSU) elections.
ABVP's Yash Dabas was elected DUSU president with 24,576 votes, defeating NSUI's Vijay Shankar Meena who received 22,523 votes.
Yash Dabas is an international-level tennis player who represented Delhi University at the Khelo India University Games and All-India University Games.
Yash Dabas completed his undergraduate degree at Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Khalsa College and is pursuing an MA in Buddhist Studies at Delhi University.
DUSU President-elect Yash Dabas announced that his first priority would be conducting a safety audit of all college hostels and paying guest accommodations.
Independent candidate Deepanshu Shokeen won the DUSU vice-presidential post with 30,615 votes, defeating ABVP's Ishu Maurya who received 16,901 votes.
Deepanshu Shokeen chose to run as an independent candidate after learning on September 11 that he was denied a ticket by NSUI.
Deepanshu Shokeen hails from Peeragarhi village in west Delhi, where his father works as a bus conductor and his mother as an Anganwadi teacher.
ABVP's Riya Chhawdi won the DUSU secretary post with 21,650 votes against NSUI's Namrata Chaudhary who received 14,869 votes.
ABVP's Lakshay Raj Singh won the joint secretary post by a margin of 837 votes against Vishesh Yadav of Samajwadi Chhatra Sabha.
The National Students' Union of India (NSUI) drew a blank in the Delhi University Students' Union central panel elections.
Voter turnout for the DUSU elections was 40.46%, compared to 39.5% in the previous year.
Union Home Minister Amit Shah congratulated ABVP, stating the victory reflects youth trust in the council's Nation First ideology.

vocab.meaning: a official group or slate of positions in an election
